newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong prefers Internet to Shakespeare.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong prefers Internet to Shakespeare.

text.p: The works of Shakespeare, Chaucer and Jane Austen have been dumped from the shelves of the British Council in Hong Kong due to a lack of popular demand.

Some 20,000 volumes of Western classical literature have had to make way for video and computer terminals for surfing the Internet after records showed no one had borrowed the books for at least a year, a council spokeswoman told Reuters on Monday.
About 10,000 books -- mainly by contemporary British authors -- remain.
"I'm a literature fan, and I personally think that reading a book is different from watching a video," the spokeswoman said. "But the bottom line is public demand."
